nodes.name: Melamine to oligomer
nodes.procedure: Melamine was firstly polymerized to generate amorphous heptazinetriazine based copolymer in the presence of CaCO3. The depolymerization procedure occurred between 450°C - 550°C.

unit_operations.name: Depolymerization onset
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: characteristic peaks of cyano groups appear at about 450°C

unit_operations.name: Complete depolymerization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: CaCO3 become weaker and finally disappear completely at 550°C

nodes.name: Salt-melt polymerization
nodes.procedure: This oligomer was further polymerized into fully condensed poly(heptazine-triazine) imides under salt-melt (LiCl/KCl) treatment.

nodes.description: Photocatalytic H2 evolution under visible light (standard conditions)
nodes.source_text: PHI/PTI presents a significantly improved activity for H2 evolution (348.5 μmol h−1), which is 7.9 times that of PHI (44 μmol h−1) and about 64 times that of melon (5.4 μmol h−1). ... the AQY was determined as 42% of PHI/PTI and 5.4% of PHI at 420 nm.

nodes.description: Photocatalytic H2 evolution with K2HPO4 mediator at 420 nm
nodes.source_text: By using of K2HPO4 (0.01 M) as artificial charge carrier mediator, the AQY of PHI/PTI can even reach 64%.

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI shows characteristic diffraction peaks of both PHI at 8° and 28° (in-plane packing and interlayer stacking of heptazine units) and PTI at 12°, 21°, 26°, 29° etc.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a presents the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of PTI, PHI and PHI/PTI. In the case of PHI/PTI, both the characteristic diffraction peaks related to PHI and PTI are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI contains C, N, O, K, Ca, Li, Cl elements; N 1s peaks at 398.7 eV (sp2 C-N=C), 400.4 eV (N-(C)3), 401.2 eV (C-N-H), binding energies between PHI and PTI indicating interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results (Figure S4 and S5) of PHI/PTI confirm the presence of elements: C, N, O, K, Ca, Li and Cl... The N 1s high-resolution XPS spectra (Figure 1b) could be deconvoluted into three peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI shows typical nanorods structure similar to PHI but smaller diameter (about 25 nm), with a few hexagonal prisms probably from PTI.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of PHI/PTI, PHI and PTI are shown in Figure 1c-e. The typical nanorods structure of PHI/PTI is similar to that of PHI, but is smaller in diameter (about 25 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI shows no noticeable change in Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area or pore volume compared to pure PHI (Table S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The porosity and surface area of the samples were recorded by using the nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms. As shown in Table S2, in comparison with pure PHI, no noticeable change in terms of surface area or pore volume...

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI shows heterojunction with lattice fringes of 1.01 nm ((10-10) plane of PHI) and 0.73 nm ((10-10) plane of PTI), forming semi-coherent interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, a heterojunction comprising two lattice fringes with distance around 1.01 nm and 0.73 nm, which are assigned to (10-10) plane of PHI and PTI...

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI element mapping confirms presence of C, N, K, O, Ca, Cl elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) analysis (Figure S9) and the element mapping images (Figure 2c) indicate that PHI/PTI comprises of C, N, K, O, Ca and Cl elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI contains K+ and Ca2+ ions close to pure PHI (~7 wt.%), few Li+ and Cl- ions indicating PTI presence (Table S3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of metal elements (K+, Li+ and Ca2+) are further measured by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) (Table S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: PHI/PTI absorption edge similar to PHI with enhanced UV absorption; band gap energy close to 2.66 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3a, the absorption edge of PHI/PTI copolymer is similar to that of PHI... The band gap energy of PHI/PTI is close to 2.66 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectra of PHI/PTI confirm presence of heptazine/triazine units (Figure S3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) and Raman spectra of PHI/PTI (Figure S3) further prove the composition of heptazine/triazine units.

nodes.characterization_summary: 13C NMR peak 3 and 15N NMR peak 2 indicate PTI component; 15N NMR peak 4 indicates PHI component in PHI/PTI (Figure S6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S6, the existence of peak 3 in 13C NMR and the peak 2 in 15N NMR spectra of PHI/PTI indicate the presence of PTI component...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of PHI/PTI confirm composition of heptazine/triazine units (Figure S3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) and Raman spectra of PHI/PTI (Figure S3) further prove the composition of heptazine/triazine units.
